name: Microsoft Xbox family
summary: Explore the original Xbox hardware revisions and five homebrew routes into the console: ENDGAME softmod is the easiest and safest entry; TSOP flashing gives a permanent BIOS mod on everything except revision 1.6, where only softmod or a modchip is possible.

specs.cpu: Intel Pentium III (Coppermine) at 733 MHz, 128 KB L2 cache
specs.gpu: NVIDIA NV2A (NV20 family) with integrated northbridge
specs.storage: 8 GB or 10 GB internal IDE hard drive, locked to the console via EEPROM key
specs.media: DVD-ROM; DVD playback requires the official playback kit dongle
specs.display: Composite/component output; 480p, 720p and 1080i on supported software

variants.notes: First retail boards. TSOP flash possible (1 MB TSOP). Softmod works on all revisions.
XBLADE board layout. 256 KB TSOP, ATX power connector, Samsung D-die RAM. TSOP flash possible but requires a DVD-R. Revision 1.5 is unconfirmed: reported sightings turned out to be 1.4 boards.
Later boards with different video encoder and power section. TSOP flashing is impossible; use a softmod or a modchip instead.

firmware.version: Microsoft Dashboard — no vendor update path; version varies by HDD contents and game disc installs

homebrew.name: ENDGAME (Xbox Softmodding Tool)
homebrew.summary: ConsoleMods calls this the easiest and safest softmod route. It needs an Xbox-to-USB adapter and a USB flash drive or Android device — no game disc is required.

compatibility.note: Works on all retail revisions per ConsoleMods; 1.6 boards skip TSOP and go straight to softmod.

requirements: An Xbox-to-USB adapter and a compatible USB flash drive or Android device.
warnings: Back up the EEPROM before any drive work; the EEPROM holds the HDD key.

homebrew.name: Game-save exploit
homebrew.firmware: All versions; requires one of six specific games
homebrew.summary: An older softmod entry that uses a save-file exploit in one of six specific games plus an Xbox-to-USB adapter. Predates ENDGAME.

compatibility.note: Only works with one of six specific game saves. ENDGAME is preferred as it needs no disc.

requirements: One of the six supported game saves, an Xbox-to-USB adapter and a USB drive.
warnings: ENDGAME is now the recommended route; this exploit is documented mainly for completeness.

homebrew.name: Modchip
homebrew.summary: A modchip replaces the stock BIOS and boots the modded dashboard directly. Works even with a dead locked drive. Some chips are solderless and suited to specific revisions.

compatibility.note: All revisions take a modchip, though some chip models are revision-specific. 1.6 boards require a modchip since TSOP flash is impossible.

requirements: A modchip for the target revision, soldering equipment (or a solderless chip model).
warnings: Soldering intervention; a bad install can brick the console without an EEPROM backup.

homebrew.name: OpenXenium
homebrew.firmware: All versions; loads a custom BIOS instead of the stock one
homebrew.summary: An open-source recreation of the Xenium modchip in GPL VHDL. It loads custom BIOS files such as Cromwell and its derivatives without modifying the onboard TSOP flash or softmodding, and provides EEPROM backup and hard-drive tools.

compatibility.note: The project README says it loads custom BIOS files without modifying the onboard TSOP flash or softmodding, so it does not depend on the revision.

requirements: An OpenXenium board (or the parts and CPLD to build one) and soldering equipment.
warnings: Soldering work on the LPC header; back up the EEPROM before any drive work.

homebrew.name: TSOP flash
homebrew.firmware: All versions except 1.6; writes a modified BIOS to the TSOP chip
homebrew.summary: Reflashes the TSOP chip with a modified BIOS, functionally equivalent to a modchip. Needs soldering and a DVD-R, or a working exploit or already-installed softmod.

compatibility.note: Revision 1.6 boards cannot be TSOP-flashed — ConsoleMods states this explicitly.

requirements: Soldering equipment, a TSOP programmer, and a DVD-R; or a working exploit/softmod.
warnings: Impossible on revision 1.6 — use softmod or modchip instead.
A bad TSOP write needs a modchip or an external programmer to recover.

homebrew.name: Linux (Xbox Linux)
homebrew.firmware: Requires a modded console; no dashboard-specific limit
homebrew.summary: A work-in-progress CD-installable Linux distribution. It is research, not a maintained general-purpose install — blocking issues remain.

compatibility.note: Xboxdevwiki lists blocking issues; it is not a turnkey distribution.

requirements: A modded Xbox and a blank CD for the installer.
warnings: Linux is unfinished; xboxdevwiki documents known blocking issues.

homebrew.name: XBMC4Gamers
homebrew.firmware: Requires a modified Xbox that can run a replacement dashboard
homebrew.summary: A dashboard front end built on XBMC4Xbox: a skin plus Python scripts for per-profile saves, artwork and game launching. The README's install step copies the built folder to the console over FTP.

compatibility.note: Installed over FTP on a modified Xbox; the README gives no revision limit.

requirements: A modified Xbox with FTP access.
warnings: It replaces the dashboard; keep the previous dashboard files so the change can be undone.

homebrew.name: Xbox system software update and reinstall
homebrew.firmware: The Microsoft Dashboard from the hard drive; no version ceiling for softmods
homebrew.summary: A stock Xbox loads its dashboard from the hard drive. The console updated from game discs while Xbox Live ran; a stock console stays on whatever dashboard it has.

compatibility.note: No vendor update path today. Modded consoles usually boot an alternative dashboard instead.

warnings: A softmod can be removed by restoring the original dashboard files and EEPROM.

communities.name: Insignia
communities.description: A free replacement for Microsoft's original Xbox Live servers: online multiplayer, leaderboards and friends for 213 supported games. Stock consoles can register through a one-time, non-permanent exploit; modded consoles run the Setup Assistant as homebrew.

officialSupport.summary: The Xbox generation is discontinued; Microsoft no longer provides hardware or system-software support.
